newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet-Telecom should sell non-core units -minister.
newsitem.headline: Stet-Telecom should sell non-core units -minister.

text.p: Italian phone operator Telecom Italia and its parent Stet, which the government plans to merge, should sell off non-core businesses and concentrate on telecoms, a Treasury minister said.

Undersecretary Filippo Cavazzuti said in an interview with financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore that the question of the industrial role of the group to be privatised was more important than the form of merger itself.
"I believe that Stet and Telecom should concentrate on fixed-line and mobile telephony, selling all the industrial activities not central to the new group," he said.
He mentioned specifically Stet's Sirti cablemaker unit, its telecoms systems manufacturer Italtel and "part of Finsiel", Stet's IT systems subsidiary.

Details of the two companies' merger are expected to be revealed this month but certain confusion has arisen recently with some government officials proposing Telecom Italia should absorb Stet and some saying it should be the reverse.
Cavazzuti said he thought it would be more logical to fuse Stet into Telecom Italia, so putting onto the market an operating company with a clearly defined core business.
Posts and Telecommunications minister Antonio Maccanico said on Monday that there were "no problems within the government" over the method of the merger.
He also said that the government aimed to approve measures to create a telecoms sector watchdog authority by March, a necessary step before Stet's privatisation due this year.
